messages:
incident-bot: Pager: High GPU queue growth detected in us-north1. Autoscaler failed to allocate GPUs (quota denied). Current queue length on inference pool: ~1.9k requests. Impact: ~12% of active requests > 10s. Pager severity: P1.

casey-oncall: seeing it. joining bridge now — starting config checks.

maria-sre: I can help. early hypothesis: region quota returned 403 from cloud quota API when trying to create GPUs; autoscaler retried and hit backoff.

casey-oncall: confirmed autoscaler logs show repeated "Quota has been exceeded" for GPU type a100-40gb in us-north1. snippet:```
2026-03-15T14:02:10Z autoscaler: createInstance failed: quotaExceeded: requested 4 GPUs but only 0 available for project
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z autoscaler: backoff 30s
```

devin-platform: tagging in. is this account global quota or regional? I see some transient frees in other regions earlier.

maria-sre: looks regional: us-north1 had a quota cap applied yesterday by cloud provider during maintenance window. Running quick check:```
gcloud compute regions describe us-north1 --project redwood-prod --format="yaml(quotas)"```
Output shows GPUs: 0/0 for a100-40gb.

jules-support: customers on trial and a few high-throughput customers are flagging increased latency via alerts. I started a quick slack DM triage with account teams. 

casey-oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) route new traffic to eu-west1/us-west2 where we have spare pool, 2) enable manual fallback to smaller instance type (v100/rtx) for lower perf but available quota, 3) request emergency quota bump with cloud provider (likely slow). Which should we execute now?

kevin-eng: we have hot path for rerouting in the gateway. Can flip route for non-sensitive customers in ~45s with no deploy. For enterprise customers pinned to us-north1 we need to respect region pinning.

devin-platform: recommend 1 + 2 for different customer sets. Start reroute for public-hosted traffic while we convert a couple of canaries to fallback instance types. I'll prepare the runbook steps.

casey-oncall: executing gateway reroute now for general pool. command:```
# toggle region weight to deprioritize us-north1
curl -X PATCH https://gateway.internal/api/route -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"region_weights": {"us-north1": 0.05, "eu-west1": 0.6, "us-west2": 0.35}}'
```

infra-bot: deploybot: traffic-shift job started by casey-oncall at 14:06:11Z. job-id: ts-4951236789.

jules-support: started customer comms draft for affected customers (non pinned): short note + ETA that we're shifting traffic and expect 30-90s improvement for most calls. pinging account managers for enterprise pinned customers.

maria-sre: starting fallback conversion on two canaries to smaller GPU instance type (rtx-6000-24gb). plan: adjust model-serving config to lower max_batch_size and reduce qps-per-instance. Patch:```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/model-pool FALLBACK_INSTANCE=rtx-6000-24gb && kubectl rollout restart deploy/model-pool -n inference
```

casey-oncall: doing quick canary for fallback on pool-a. will monitor queue.

maria-sre: canary reports: tail latency reduced from 18s -> 6s for fallback requests, but tokenization cost increases. Good to expand if stable.

devin-platform: I also kicked off emergency support request to cloud account team. Ticket created: CLOUD-84217 (requested temporary regional GPU quota increase). Estimated response ETA: 30-90 minutes. Not reliable for immediate mitigation.

casey-oncall: action summary so far: traffic shift to other regions (partial), fallback instance canaries started, cloud quota request opened, customer comms drafted. Impact: total queued requests dropped from 1.9k -> 300 in 4 minutes after route change.

jules-support: monitoring support queue — a few customers reported degraded image-generation throughput; most see improvements after reroute.

kevin-eng: note: autoscaler still logs failures when it tries to scale in us-north1; we should stop autoscaler for that pool to avoid noisy errors and exponential backoff causing retry storms. Recommend scale target=0 and mark pool drained.

casey-oncall: setting autoscaler min=0 for us-north1 pools.```
gcloud compute autoscaler update my-inference-autoscaler --region us-north1 --min-num-replicas 0 --project redwood-prod
```

infra-bot: autoscaler update acknowledged.

maria-sre: confirmed. suppressing alert rules for that pool to avoid pager fatigue. Will keep P1 open until all pinned traffic stable.

devin-platform: manual mitigation checklist posted to runbook channel:```
- shift gateway weights away from affected region
- convert canaries to fallback instance type
- scale down autoscaler in affected region to 0 to stop noise
- open cloud quota escalation ticket
- prepare multi-region failover for pinned customers (requires account ok)
```

casey-oncall: metrics update: overall 95th latency back to baseline for non-pinned traffic. Pinned (us-north1) customers still experiencing 5-12s extra latency; two customers report transient failures.

jules-support: drafting individual messages for the two impacted enterprise customers with proposed mitigation and estimated resolution timeline (depends on cloud response or consent for multi-region migration).

kevin-eng: small optimization: enable KV prefix caching for pinned customers so we can reduce QPS to instances. I can toggle cache TTL for specific routes. That might reduce pressure without moving them.

maria-sre: good call — please do that for the top-3 impacted tenants.

kevin-eng: toggled KV cache TTL 300s for tenant:acme-corp, tenant:orbit-ml, tenant:fastphoto.

ops-runbook-bot: runbook note appended by casey-oncall at 14:18Z: "us-north1 quota-exhaustion — applied partial regional reroute, started fallback canaries, autoscaler paused; cloud ticket CLOUD-84217 opened."

casey-oncall: tagging @maria-sre to hand off on-call in 25 minutes. Will leave the bridge to you. Summary: main mitigations applied, queue largely drained for non-pinned, two enterprise customers need org-level decisions.

maria-sre: taking over on-call. I'll keep bridge open and follow cloud ticket. Assigning priority: continue traffic shift, expand fallback if we see requeue growth, pursue quota bump and/or customer consent for multi-region failover.

jules-support: I'm staying on the thread for customer comms.

casey-oncall: leaving bridge. @maria-sre — over to you. :white_check_mark: 

maria-sre: noted. next updates: will post if cloud replies or if we get requeue >500. scheduling follow-ups every 10m.

infra-bot: ticket CLOUD-84217 status: acknowledged by cloud support, priority: expedited. assigned engineer: cloud-eng-rosa.

maria-sre: after 12m the cloud engineer replied asking for usage justification and expected decommission time. I sent current metrics and proposed timeline to release pressure in 6-12 hours.

jules-support: customers acknowledged communications; two will accept temporary multi-region routing under a support agreement, one wants hold in-region only — they are an enterprise compliance case.

maria-sre: plan for next 60m: expand fallback to full non-enterprise pool, keep autoscaler paused in us-north1, continue cloud follow-up. If cloud approves quota bump, we'll re-enable autoscaler and scale gradually.

kevin-eng: adding an item: create a short-term alert rule to notify if any region's GPU quota drops to 0 (automated shotcall) so we can act faster next time.

maria-sre: noted. adding to runbook. final note: this incident impacted latency but we avoided full outage by shifting and fallbacks. Will keep thread updated.

ops-runbook-bot: incident P1 downgraded to P2 at 15:02Z after stabilization for most traffic; enterprise pinned cases remain open for follow-up.

maria-sre: handing off formally to follow-up rotation @kevin-eng at 18:00Z for postmortem tracking. Closing live-bridge now.

kevin-eng: acknowledged. I'll capture timeline and RCA input.

jules-support: will send final customer summary and post-incident comms draft in #customer-ops.

incident-bot: Incident closed (live mitigation). Reference: INC-4951236789.
